works.title: Channel Zilch
works.status: Published 2013 · ~100k words · Author-read audiobook (67 chapter takes) in the vault
works.logline: A washed-out NASA astronaut is recruited by an eccentric tycoon and his brilliant, terrifying punk daughter to steal the display shuttle Enterprise, smuggle it across the world, mate it to a black-market Soviet Energia, and launch it — the first step in privately kickstarting the Singularity.
works.summary: Mick Oolfson, disgraced ex-shuttle-pilot turned manure crop-duster, gets THE CALL from tycoon Manuel Chin. The catch: the spacecraft is Enterprise, NASA's engineless museum shuttle. Mick falls hard for Chin's daughter Heloise — green-eyed, belly-LED, gleefully amoral riot-grrrl genius — and signs on. A comic heist (Chin piggybacked as a robe-wearing GIANT WITH A GUN), a shuttle-on-jumbo aerial getaway through the Bull Run Mountains, a globe-crossing smuggling odyssey to Baikonur, thruster-blasting past gangster roadblocks — ending mid-launch under Boss Delp's machine-gun fire: Back into the wild black yonder! Continued in Hel's Bet.
works.themes: The Dream of Space as secular salvation; renegade vs. institutional spaceflight; the Singularity; obsession as virtue and pathology; underdog redemption for pilot and shuttle alike.

works.title: Hel's Bet
works.status: Published 2015 · ~120k words
works.logline: Having stolen Enterprise, the crew reaches orbit — where the real ordeal begins: a NASA capture mission, months of claustrophobic orbital siege, Hel's escalating and disturbing genius, and a malignant distributed-AI threat grown in a gangster's mind-farm.
works.summary: Opens on the exact line Book 1 ended on. Enterprise mates with Boojum (a purple server-farm module) and wins a judo duel with the pursuing shuttle Atlantis. Then the long orbital siege: boredom, Earth-watching, a missed resupply tug, rationing, cabin fever. Hel HAL-jacks the ship (checkmate, starchild); Mick out-hacks her with a literal cable swap. The Zombie Meatnet — an evil, scalable group-mind extortion scheme from the Gogol syndicate — emerges, plus a hostile takeover of a Russian space company. Climax: a sabotaged EVA, a jammed container detonating, a punctured xenon tank. Title = Pascal's Wager 2.0: bet on the Singularity or accept a taste for dirt.
works.themes: The Singularity as Pascal's Wager; benevolent vs. malignant emergent AI; genius unmoored from ethics; confinement and crew psychology; mortality and legacy.

works.title: Castle Rising
works.status: Complete draft, query-ready · ~50k words · Great Games Galaxy #1
works.logline: In 1147, a godlike alien collector plucks four children — each from a different real human civilization — out of their homes along with their cultures' architectural treasures, and forces them through a gauntlet of video-game-like trials aboard its vast ship.
works.summary: Zbu (a living tripod of recursively nested swords) and its vapor-speaking bubble-servants the Greetz seize 27 architectural marvels and one child with each. Four become the heart of the book: Shenkasa, bold one-eyed princess of Great Zimbabwe; Visel, giggling super-jumper enslaved soldier from Angkor Wat; Will, a timid trans autistic scribe-in-training from Castle Rising, England; and Magpie, a sage apprentice feather-merchant from Mesa Verde who bonds minds with birds — a prodigy who forces Zbu to rebalance the games. Solo bubble-escapes give way to team trials, animal companions, and earned superhuman gifts. Hopeful, kinetic, deliberately multicultural.
works.themes: Coming-of-age and courage; cross-cultural empathy and teamwork; disability, neurodivergence, and trans identity portrayed heroically; play as a crucible of growth; wonder over fear.

works.title: Cold Fronts
works.status: Complete 2019 · produced by Doug; authored by a relative
works.logline: The career memoir of a professional USAF meteorologist whose service threads through the major theaters and technologies of the Cold War — from 1950s overseas weather posts to the birth of military weather and spy satellites.
works.summary: From Midwest origins through North African postings (Sidi Slimane's boredom, athletics, and radar tests that couldn't tell the Sixth Fleet from an Italian fishing fleet), through Sputnik and the space race, into the book's technical heart: pioneering software on the UNIVAC 418 — inventing memory overlays to make a tiny computer effectively unlimited — feeding the DMSP weather satellites whose real-time imagery served Vietnam operations and the covert spy-satellite program. Ends with moving reflections on defending his drafted young airmen from Vietnam-era protesters' scorn.
works.themes: Duty and the cost of freedom; science and national security wed; institutional secrecy and need-to-know; family across a mobile military life; generational conflict over Vietnam.

works.title: Brainrot for AIs
works.status: Source manuscript · keystone nonfiction · sensitive
works.logline: Doug's project to make a book from years of voice notes about living with Central Pain Syndrome — framed explicitly as a collaboration with an AI, because ordering things is one of the abilities the condition took.
works.summary: A tagged mosaic of transcribed voice memos: the phenomenology of a brain where sensation is rerouted to pain; candid self-debugging of cognitive loss; endurance and meaning; small counterweight pleasures — cold air on skin, distant birdcalls; clinical intake transcripts; the friends who keep him going. The central image: the me organ, a brain sliding along hot concrete. The book's form enacts its subject — it can't be written in order, so it's assembled from fragments.
works.themes: Chronic neuropathic pain; the self as fragile organ; cognitive disability; the will to keep creating; AI as cognitive prosthetic; gallows humor as survival.

works.title: Less Alone
works.status: Complete draft 2018 · compiled/edited by Doug
works.logline: A book assembled from the real Facebook posts, poems, and conversations of Philip Watson — living with Central Pain Syndrome — his wife Isla, and the community of friends who answered him: suffering shared is suffering made less alone.
works.summary: Doug gathered and arranged the posts of a man whose brain injury stripped memory and self and whose CPS renders warmth as ice and acid. Isla's steady tenderness forms the spine; a chorus of co-author friends answers each post; later essays test his identity against Eysenck and Phineas Gage. The book wears its collaborative seams openly — early-reader notes, unsettled chapter order — and enacts its own argument in form.
works.themes: Chronic pain's lived reality; identity after brain injury; love as medicine; community and witness; dignity and humor under unrelenting pain.

works.title: Frankfurt to Grindelwald
works.status: Complete · short piece
works.logline: A young exchange student's hash-hazed 1974 hitchhike across Europe toward a long-planned romantic rendezvous nearly collapses when he swaps passports with his travel buddy at the Swiss border — and everything comes down to whether the mail beats Easter.
works.summary: Oxford, spring 1974: Doug and his cannabis-teetotaler buddy Paul thumb from Rhein-Main Air Base into a Cadillac of airmen with a skull-carved meerschaum pipe, then a BMW hyperjump down the Autobahn. Thoroughly stoned at the Swiss border, Doug hands back the wrong passports. At the Grindelwald hostel — facing the Eiger's Mordwand — his Oxford scholar has serendipitously appeared; alpine kisses ensue. Then the morning passport ritual exposes the swap. Express mail vs. Good Friday shutdown, with the Getty kidnapping as the omen. Thursday's last delivery: THE PASSPORT. This story had a happy ending, but a gentleman does not tell.
works.themes: Youthful wanderlust; the golden age of European hitchhiking; comic catastrophe from one stoned mistake; nostalgia for a pre-cellphone Cold-War Europe.

works.title: Sweatshop in the Sky
works.status: Complete 2021 · with Sandy Matthews
works.logline: A savage Swiftian farce: a cartoon Jeff Bezos races Musk and Branson to be First Billionaire in Outer Space, then builds an orbital Amazon fulfillment center worked by human Serfs railgunned into orbit in edible goo.
works.summary: Written as gleefully bad pulp packed with Tom Swifties. A Muskbot bomb strands the Bezos brothers an inch and a quarter below Outer Space; a Peruvian railgun launches vitrified workers at only 55g; the Borg-cube Amazon von Braun Space Fulfillment Center runs on debt peonage, shock-collar JetBelts, and Alexa. The heart: Serf #23,458's furious interior monologue against the chipper corporate tour voice. She accidentally frees every Serf's joystick, cries Union — and Bezos vents the station's air, killing 40,000, before setting course to buy the Sun from God. Opens with real NYT/WaPo excerpts on Amazon warehouses, so the cartoon lands on fact.
works.themes: Billionaire space vanity; Amazon labor exploitation; surveillance capitalism; union-busting; the gulf between corporate PR language and worker reality.

works.title: Xmas Prime
works.status: Published 2020 · art integral (8MB PDF)
works.logline: An illustrated satire delivering the interior monologue of Serf #23,458 grinding through the Xmas Prime rush in Bezos's orbital fulfillment center — the Sweatshop material distilled to its bleakest, funniest core and given pictures.
works.summary: Subtitle: A Primitive AI Gibbers about Sociopathic Capitalism and Jeff Bezos. The dual-register engine at full power: the sunny corporate wake-up call against her one-word answer; the Rate quotas, pain-penalty shocks, the jammed Sphincter, and a nightly ledger that leaves her deeper in debt for the air she breathes. Sibling to Sweatshop in the Sky — same world, same target, illustration-forward. (Deep text pass still owed from the archive .docx.)
works.themes: Warehouse labor exploitation; algorithmic control; debt peonage; Christmas consumerism as the crunch that grinds workers hardest.

works.title: The Gospel of John with Werewolf
works.status: Complete 2019 · Withered Branch Press · audiobook by Vince Gauthier-Bradner
works.logline: A Howl Against Anti-Semitism: the Gospel of John rewritten as an absurd canine Doggoland burlesque and set against John's actual King James text — framed by a serious, documented argument that John is the Bible's engine of anti-Jewish violence.
works.summary: Thesis stated flat: No Gospel of John, no Holocaust. The foreword traces the Christ-killer libel from John's verses through Passion-play mobs, Luther's On the Jews and Their Lies, Nazi admiration at Nuremberg, to the 2019 Poway synagogue shooter quoting John. Then the weapon: Jesus becomes Werewolf, Alpha Schnauzer Trainer and Laser Pointer of Doggoland; scripture is Whiz mark; the Passion ends when He gave up the Frisbee — desecration-by-silliness beside the real text with its lethal passages highlighted in blood. Two registers in violent, deliberate contrast.
works.themes: Scriptural roots of antisemitism; sacred texts as engines of real-world violence; satire and blasphemy as moral protest; the John-to-Luther-to-Holocaust throughline.

works.title: Palin/Cheney 2012
works.status: Draft ~13,900 words · with Casey Muratori · part prose, part outline
works.logline: A Right-Wing Nightmare: an alternate 2012 where a Palin/Cheney ticket rides a domestic terror catastrophe into total power, then spirals through privatized authoritarianism, foreign invasion, and apocalypse.
works.summary: A bored, magnificently profane bunker-Cheney engineers Palin's comeback and stages a convention terror rescue. Then the Westboro Phelps Gang dirty-bombs 13 cities and nukes D.C. the night before the election; sole survivor Clarence Thomas validates the vote. Palin resigns at her inauguration as Queen Esther; President Cheney privatizes the entire government, nukes Albuquerque, and provokes a ChIranian invasion authorized in language mirroring the Iraq War resolution. Erik Prince sells the military to the higher bidder, massacres the cabinet, and installs Limbaugh/Coulter. Ends on the carrier under MISSION ACCOMPLISHED as the world burns.
works.themes: Authoritarian collapse; apocalyptic religion fused with state power; torture's boomerang; mercenary capitalism with no loyalty but profit; righteous certainty indicted.

works.title: Fuck the Virus / Online Dating
works.status: Two assembled works · privacy-sensitive
works.logline: Found literature built verbatim from Doug's real online-dating life: a 2004 found novella of profiles, messages, and editorial stage-directions, and its COVID-era sibling assembled from the pandemic app landscape.
works.summary: Artist with Lake Cabin seeks Passionate Woman. The novella reproduces Doug's real 2004 profile plus the answering chorus of midwestern longing and his own running notes. The art is in selection and sequencing: an accidental narrative of a disabled artist seeking connection at a hinge point in his life. F%ck The Virus repeats the method across OkCupid/Tinder/Bumble/Feeld in the COVID era.
works.themes: Loneliness and connection; honesty vs. self-marketing; disability and desirability; the vocabulary of dating platforms; documentary collage as truth-telling.
